reason: E1 supports the competition between work hardening and dynamic recovery in a similar RHEA, but only E2 addresses elastic/plastic anisotropy in BCC materials, not thermal expansion mismatch or internal stresses. The key premises about thermal expansion mismatch generating internal stresses and causing non-monotonic property trends are not supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Work hardening and dynamic recovery/recrystallization compete during high-temperature deformation of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Pre-deformation (cold rolling) introduces high dislocation density that enhances work hardening.
Thermal expansion mismatch between grains generates internal stresses in polycrystalline BCC alloys.
Internal stresses from thermal expansion mismatch can counteract softening at elevated temperatures.
The balance between dislocation hardening and recovery produces non-monotonic yield strength and modulus trends with temperature.
